claims: Monitor electrolyte levels, particularly potassium and chloride.
Continue mechanical ventilation with settings adjusted for patient comfort and respiratory status.
Assess and manage pain appropriately, given moderate pain reported.
Monitor arterial blood gases and pH to ensure adequate oxygenation and ventilation.
Consider fluid management, given low sodium and chloride levels.
Monitor coagulation parameters, including INR and PT, due to prolonged bleeding time.
Continue close monitoring of renal function, indicated by low creatinine levels.
Evaluate and manage anemia, indicated by low hemoglobin and hematocrit levels.
Monitor heart rate and rhythm, indicated by arrhythmia settings on the pacemaker.
Ensure proper skin and wound care to prevent complications.

facts.claim_text: Continue mechanical ventilation with settings adjusted for patient comfort and respiratory status.
facts.text: The patient is currently on mechanical ventilation.

facts.label: not_supported
facts.reason: The last ventilator/intubation record ('Peak Insp. Pressure: 27 cmH2O') was 19.5 h before the decision, with none after it. Ventilator settings are charted every 1-4 h while ventilated, so by the rule (> 6 h without a record) the patient was not ventilated at T.
